method: Conservatively curated ISM control-to-ATT&CK mitigation bridges. Expansion through official ATT&CK mitigates relationships is discovery-only; it does not create candidates or mappings.

bridges.rationale: The controls require timely application and operating-system patching, which directly supports ATT&CK Update Software mitigation guidance.

evidence.note: Literal patching requirements; effectiveness remains implementation- and technique-dependent.

bridges.rationale: The controls harden or restrict executable features and system configuration, supporting ATT&CK Disable or Remove Feature or Program guidance in their stated scope.

evidence.note: Contextual hardening bridge; individual technique applicability requires review.

bridges.rationale: The controls enable memory integrity and Local Security Authority protection, supporting ATT&CK Privileged Process Integrity guidance for protecting high-integrity processes.

evidence.note: Privileged-process integrity bridge; individual technique edges remain candidates.

bridges.rationale: The controls require application control or trusted execution restrictions, directly supporting ATT&CK Execution Prevention guidance.

evidence.note: Literal application-control bridge; broad downstream relationships require exact review.

bridges.rationale: The controls provide security-control ruleset assurance or centralized collection and review of security-relevant events, supporting ATT&CK Audit guidance as a detection-oriented effect.

evidence.note: Ruleset assurance and audit evidence can support detection; they do not themselves prevent technique execution.

bridges.rationale: The controls enforce hardened security settings for Microsoft Office, PDF software, and web browsers, supporting ATT&CK Software Configuration guidance.

evidence.note: Broad configuration bridge constrained to each control's stated scope.

bridges.rationale: The controls constrain access to or operation of unsafe behaviors, supporting ATT&CK Behavior Prevention on Endpoint guidance.

evidence.note: Endpoint behavior prevention is contextual; technique edges remain candidates.

bridges.rationale: The control enables antivirus scanning of Microsoft Office macros, supporting ATT&CK Antivirus or Antimalware guidance.

evidence.note: Office macro antivirus-scanning bridge.

bridges.rationale: The control requires macros to be checked for malicious code before signing or placement in Trusted Locations, supporting ATT&CK Code Signing guidance.

evidence.note: Constrain effect selected because the control does not categorically prevent execution.

bridges.rationale: The controls restrict write access to Trusted Locations and permissions to modify or delete event logs, supporting ATT&CK Restrict File and Directory Permissions guidance for those paths.

evidence.note: Permissions and integrity bridge covering trusted macro locations and event logs.

bridges.rationale: The controls restrict Microsoft Office macro enablement to Trusted Locations or macros signed by trusted publishers, supporting ATT&CK Code Signing guidance.

evidence.note: Signed-code requirement; exact technique applicability requires review.

bridges.rationale: The control blocks web browsers from processing advertisements from the internet, supporting ATT&CK Restrict Web-Based Content guidance.

evidence.note: Internet-advertisement blocking bridge.

bridges.rationale: The controls reduce standing privilege and separate privileged administration, supporting ATT&CK Privileged Account Management guidance.

evidence.note: Broad privilege bridge with a constrain effect; 112 downstream relationships require exact review.

bridges.rationale: The controls restrict privileged and unprivileged account logons across their respective operating environments, supporting ATT&CK Account Use Policies guidance.

evidence.note: Cross-boundary operating-environment logon policy bridge.

bridges.rationale: The control requires administrative activity to pass through jump servers with limited network access, supporting ATT&CK Limit Access to Resource Over Network guidance.

evidence.note: Network-resource exposure is constrained rather than categorically prevented.

bridges.rationale: The controls explicitly require multi-factor authentication, directly supporting ATT&CK Multi-factor Authentication guidance.

evidence.note: Literal MFA requirements; effectiveness still depends on factor and flow resistance.

bridges.rationale: The control requires credentials to be long, unique, unpredictable, and managed, supporting ATT&CK Password Policies guidance.

evidence.note: Credential-quality and management policy bridge.

bridges.rationale: The controls explicitly require Microsoft Defender Credential Guard, directly supporting ATT&CK Credential Access Protection guidance.

evidence.note: Literal Credential Guard requirements.

bridges.rationale: The controls require recoverable backups, directly supporting ATT&CK Data Backup guidance as a recovery effect.

evidence.note: Backup requirements reduce impact and support recovery; they do not prevent initial execution.

bridges.rationale: The controls protect backup isolation, access, retention, and testing, supporting ATT&CK Data Backup guidance by constraining impact.

evidence.note: Backup-protection bridge; constrain effect separates resilience from prevention.

bridges.rationale: The controls explicitly require vulnerability scanning, directly supporting ATT&CK Vulnerability Scanning guidance as exposure detection.

evidence.note: Detect means detecting exposures, not detecting adversary behavior.
